claim.public_wording: An account of SwimSignal's forecast model, not of measured bacteria. For each monitored storm overflow it counts the days in a past bathing season when the model would have put a listed swim spot at its high level with this overflow and below high without it. Where the EA's spill record is usable the overflow's spill days are the recorded ones; elsewhere they are modelled from rain. The weights, the travel times and the levels are the model's. No sample is used.
not_claimed: that any spot-day had bad water, or any sample result
any share of the bacteria at a spot: the figures do not add up to a spot's days
that any overflow or company broke a permit or a rule
how much any overflow discharged: a recorded spill day is 1 however long the spill
any comparison or ranking of companies
that the model's level is right: travel times, dilution and the levels are the model's settings
that a spot the table leaves out is clean, or that an overflow it leaves out reaches no swimmer

evidence.text: At 59 river points no model here had seen, the production estimate put a point's days in order with a within-point correlation of 0.376. Rain in the last 48 hours alone gave 0.355. So the overflow chain adds little to the order at rivers.

definitions.season: 15 May to 30 September, local days (Europe/London), 139 days. 2025 is the headline; 2024 shows the spread.
definitions.recorded: 1 on a UTC day the EA start/stop file holds an event at the overflow (features.spill_days, the model's training label), placed on the local day of the same date; else 0.
definitions.usable: A record is used for a season when the company's EA file for that year covers the season, the year's return gives EDM operational 90% or more, and the file holds an event at it that year or the return gives 0 spills that year.
definitions.modelled: The production spill model's lead-0 calibrated chance on archive rain, with the covariates of the return of the year before, by CATCH-SIM's Hindcast.
definitions.runs: recorded: run A, recorded states where usable and modelled chances elsewhere (the headline). modelled: run B, modelled chances throughout.
definitions.level: The page's level from the shown score: low under 15, moderate under 40, high under 70, else very high.
definitions.high: The season figure: spot-days at high or very high with every overflow and below high with this overflow's state set to 0 on every day (CATCH-SIM's removal rule), added over the spots it reaches. Spot-days.
definitions.moderate: Spot-days at moderate or above with every overflow and low with this overflow taken out.
definitions.lowered: Spot-days whose level falls at all with this overflow taken out.
definitions.high_no_single: A spot's high days that no single removal brings below high: they need two or more overflows out.
definitions.not_additive: An overflow's figure is not a share. A day that needs two overflows counts at each; a day that several overflows each reach alone counts at none. The figures at a spot do not sum to its days.
definitions.spill_days: Recorded spill days in the season, where the record is usable; null elsewhere, never 0.
definitions.expected_days: The sum of the modelled daily chances over the season's days, for every overflow.

reproduction.rule: Run B at Cromwheel and Waterhead against CATCH-SIM's committed series: every level equal, every shown score within 1, at least 99% equal

comparison.note: Descriptive, deciding nothing. United Utilities is in-sample: the model was fitted on its 2023-25 spills. The other companies' spills were never in the model's fit, but earlier tests here saw them.
